QuestionStmt.S: With usual notations, in a triangle $ABC$, if $\theta$ is any real number, then $a \cos(B - \theta) + b \cos(A + \theta)$ is

Solution.S:
$$a \cos(B - \theta) + b \cos(A + \theta)$$

$$= a(\cos B \cos \theta + \sin B \sin \theta) + b(\cos A \cos \theta - \sin A \sin \theta)$$

$$= a \cos B \cos \theta + a \sin B \sin \theta + b \cos A \cos \theta - b \sin A \sin \theta$$

$$= \cos \theta(a \cos B + b \cos A) + \sin \theta(a \sin B - b \sin A)$$

$$= \cos \theta \left[ \frac{a(a^2 + c^2 - b^2)}{2ac} + \frac{b(b^2 + c^2 - a^2)}{2bc} \right] + \sin \theta(abk - abk) \ldots \text{[By cosine and sine rule]}$$

$$= \cos \theta \left( \frac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2 + b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2c} \right)$$

$$= c \cos \theta$$
